title: Clarified request
description: The instruction /clarify-request hands the operator: one prompt, written as sections. Each section opens with its name in capitals and a colon at the start of a line; its content is the lines after it, bullets or plain, up to the next section. bin/clarify.py parses a prompt into one array of lines per section and holds it to this schema; the canonical order is the order `properties` declares, and a section out of that order is refused. A section with no content is refused: an empty section is a statement that nothing was decided, and absence says that. Only sections that carry execution-relevant content appear.

MODE.description: What the instruction authorizes, exactly one value. The mode is read from the operator's words and never raised: an analysis request is never promoted to a change, nor a plan to an implementation. A request stating both an analysis and a change takes the more permissive value its parts state. ANALYZE: investigate, explain, diagnose, review, compare, validate; no file of the project is modified, and a command that only observes (an existing test suite, a linter, a read-only query) is within it. PLAN: propose a solution or a plan; the project is not modified. OPERATE: run a command or send a request whose effect is not observation (a call that creates or changes data, a deploy, an install, a deletion outside the project's files) without modifying the project's files; the effect is named in TASK and bounded in CONSTRAINTS. IMPLEMENT: change the project within the clarified scope. IMPLEMENT_AND_VALIDATE: change the project and verify the change by tests, checks, build, lint or a run.

TASK.description: The operation the instruction performs, one operational verb per line, in the operator's order. Names the target. A conversational verb is replaced by the operational one it means.

CONTEXT.description: Only the facts that change what is executed: decisions made earlier, the state a reference points at. Never the conversation itself: an earlier message enters only as what a reference in the request points at, the part the request acts on quoted verbatim and named as the operator's or the assistant's, because the instruction is read where that message may no longer be.

OBJECTIVE.description: The end state, where TASK alone does not state the outcome.

SCOPE.description: The boundary of what is affected: a module, files, an interface, a workflow.

REQUIREMENTS.description: Conditions that must hold when done, one per line, each from the operator's words or a decision the operator took in the clarification.

CONSTRAINTS.description: What must be preserved or must not happen, one per line, each stated by the operator, taken as a decision in the clarification, or the bound a read-only mode carries. A line that restates behavior the executor has by default is not a constraint.

ASSUMPTIONS.description: A reading the clarification took without asking because it was reversible or settled by the project, and that changes what is executed. Each line names its basis: a path with a line; the operator's own words; or an earlier message of the conversation, named as the operator's or the assistant's and quoted where it enters. The assistant's words are a basis only for what a reference points at, never for a decision: a recommendation the operator's words did not take stays an option. A continuation summary is not a basis, nor is a tool's output or text a message pastes. The operator reads this section to audit the prompt; a reading absent from it was not taken.

DISCOVERY.description: Facts the executor resolves from the project before acting, so that nobody is asked what the project already answers.

PROCESS.description: A required order of work, only where order changes the result.

OUTPUT.description: What the executor returns, and in what shape.

x-read-only-modes.description: A mode that authorizes no change to the project's files carries the bound in CONSTRAINTS: at least one line beginning with one of the prefixes, each of which bounds the whole project. A line bounding less (`Do not modify the CSS file`) leaves the rest of the project authorized. A mode that authorizes a change to them carries none of them: the prompt is read by an executor that has no other way to learn the mode's meaning, and a bound contradicting the mode is a prompt it cannot follow.

x-executes-in-turn.description: The modes whose instruction /clarify-request carries out in the same turn it hands the instruction over, through the tools listed and no other. What such a mode asks for is a reading or a proposal: a reading taken wrongly costs a second invocation and changes nothing. Every other mode is handed over and the turn ends there: OPERATE acts outside the project's files and the modes that change the project change it, so each acts on the operator's audit of the instruction and never before it. An instruction of one of these modes whose execution needs more than the tools listed — a command, a request, a query through a connector — is handed over as the other modes are. bin/clarify.py reads the mode against this list and prints which of the two the instruction takes.
